questions.question: In an optimization model for a production plan, what is a constraint?
options: The quantity that the plan should make as large as possible
A given number, such as the hours a machine is available
A requirement that every allowed plan has to satisfy
The value a decision variable takes in the best plan

questions.question: A model must ensure that a customer's order of 30 tonnes is fully delivered, where $x$ is the number of tonnes delivered. Which type of constraint expresses this minimum requirement?
options: No constraint; it belongs in the objective

questions.question: Which of these verbal requirements on weekly production $x$ (units) calls for an equality constraint rather than an inequality?
options: No more than 400 units can be produced in a week
Exactly 400 units must be produced, as contracted
At least 400 units must be produced to meet demand
Roughly 400 units should be produced in a week

questions.question: A model has four constraints. A proposed plan satisfies three of them comfortably but breaks the fourth by a small amount. Is the plan allowed?
options: Yes; satisfying most of the constraints is sufficient
Yes, if the fourth constraint is the least important one
No; an allowed plan must satisfy every constraint with room to spare
No; every single constraint has to hold for an allowed plan

questions.question: Product 1 needs 3 machine hours per unit and product 2 needs 4. At most 120 machine hours are available. With $x_1,x_2$ the units made, which constraint expresses the machine limit?
A model has the constraints $2x_1+x_2\le10$, $x_1+3x_2\ge9$ and $x_1-x_2=1$. Which plan $(x_1,x_2)$ satisfies all three?
A modeller multiplies the constraint $-2x_1+3x_2\ge-6$ by $-1$. Which constraint results?
A model has constraint 1: $4x_1+7x_2+x_3\le30$ and constraint 2: $2x_1+5x_2+6x_3\le25$. In the notation $a_{ij}$ for the coefficient of $x_j$ in constraint $i$, what is $a_{23}$?
With $x_A$ and $x_B$ the tonnes of two products, the requirement is that $x_A$ must be at least twice $x_B$. Which linear constraint expresses this?

A workshop has 80 carpentry hours available per week, and $h(\boldsymbol{x})$ is the number of carpentry hours a plan $\boldsymbol{x}$ uses. Why is the limit written as $h(\boldsymbol{x})\le80$ rather than $h(\boldsymbol{x})=80$?
options: An equality would be less precise than the inequality
The $\le$ form ensures that at least 80 hours are used
Both forms allow the same plans, so either is fine
Fewer than 80 hours may be used; more may not be used

questions.question: A modeller rewrites the requirement $3x_1+2x_2\ge12$ as $-3x_1-2x_2\le-12$. How do the plans allowed by the rewritten constraint compare with those allowed before?
options: They are exactly the plans that broke it before
They are fewer, since the new bound is now negative
They are exactly the plans that were allowed before
None, since a right-hand side cannot be negative

questions.question: A model contains the equality $x_1+x_2=10$. Which pair of inequalities allows exactly the same plans?
options: $x_1+x_2\le10$ on its own, as the upper limit

questions.question: A blend uses $x_A$ kg of ingredient A and $x_B$ kg of ingredient B. At most 30% of the blend's weight may be ingredient A. Which linear constraint expresses this?
A shop starts the month with 20 units in stock, produces $x$ units and sells 35 units; $s$ is the end-of-month stock. Which constraint correctly links $x$ and $s$?
Product 1 takes 20 minutes and product 2 takes 45 minutes on a press that is available for 6 hours. With $x_1,x_2$ the units made, which constraint expresses the press limit?
A model's allowed plans are those satisfying constraints $C_1$, $C_2$ and $C_3$. A fourth constraint $C_4$ is added. Which statement about the new set of allowed plans is always true?
options: Some plans can become allowed that were not before
Every plan allowed now was also allowed before
Every plan allowed before is still allowed now
The number of allowed plans must strictly decrease

questions.question: A modeller replaces the two constraints $x_1\le3$ and $x_2\le5$ by the single constraint $x_1+x_2\le8$. What is the effect on the allowed plans?
options: No effect, since the sum constraint is the two constraints added
Plans such as $(6,0)$ become allowed although $x_1\le3$ forbade them
Fewer plans are allowed, since one constraint now bounds both
Both versions forbid $(6,0)$, so nothing important changes

questions.question: In a feed model, $x_1$ and $x_2$ are kilograms of two feeds containing 5 and 2 grams of protein per kilogram. The model contains the constraint $-5x_1-2x_2\le-40$. Which requirement does it express?
options: The mix must contain at least 40 g of protein
The mix may contain at most 40 g of protein
The mix must weigh at least 40 kg in total
Each feed must supply at least 40 g of protein

questions.question: Plans must satisfy $x_1\le4$, $x_2\le3$, $x_1+x_2\le10$, $2x_1+x_2\le9$, $x_1\ge0$ and $x_2\ge0$. Which constraint can be removed without changing the set of allowed plans?
